text: When the glass falls low, prepare for a blow.
provenance: Traditional barometer rhyme, unattributed. Quoted and interpreted by meteorologist Jeff Haby (theweatherprediction.com/wxlore/j/).

text: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight; red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed on the Royal Meteorological Society's MetLink weather folklore page (metlink.org).

text: When the wind is out of the east, 'tis neither good for man nor beast.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed on MetLink weather folklore (metlink.org).

text: Rain before seven, fine before eleven.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Discussed on The Natural Navigator weather lore page (naturalnavigator.com/the-library/weather-lore/).

text: Dew on the grass, no rain will come to pass.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Discussed on The Natural Navigator weather lore page (naturalnavigator.com/the-library/weather-lore/).

text: When the bees crowd into their hive again, it is a sign of thunder and of rain.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Quoted on The Natural Navigator weather lore page (naturalnavigator.com/the-library/weather-lore/).

text: Mackerel sky, mackerel sky, never long wet, never long dry.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed on the Old Farmer's Almanac weather proverbs page (almanac.com).

text: Hen scarts and filly tails make lofty ships wear low sails.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed on the Old Farmer's Almanac weather proverbs page (almanac.com).

text: Evening red and morning gray are sure signs of a fine day.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed on the Old Farmer's Almanac weather proverbs page (almanac.com).

text: If a circle forms 'round the moon, 'twill rain soon.
provenance: Traditional, unattributed. Listed in a published weather lore roundup (arlenestaffordwilson.wordpress.com, 2025); the Old Farmer's Almanac also notes the moon-halo saying.
